text: Chimerical describes a hope or dream that is imagined rather than realistic and will probably never come true. It comes from the Chimera, a monster of Greek myth that never existed. Here the film honours big dreams but sees that some may be impossible fantasies.

Quixotic means idealistic in a way that is impractical. It comes from Don Quixote, the Spanish novel's hero who charged at windmills thinking they were giants. Here it describes broke Stallone refusing huge offers unless he could star in his own script.

Avowedly means openly, by the person's own admission. It comes from avow, to declare something openly. Here the three-day writing story is what Stallone himself says, part of the legend around the film.
Chitty Chitty Bang Bang is a 1968 family musical film about a magical car. The article uses it as an example of a classic that people misremember: the car does not start flying until halfway through.
Jaws is a 1975 thriller about a giant shark terrorising a beach town. The article notes it is also very funny, another classic that is remembered only for its scary moments.
Misremembered means remembered wrongly or in a distorted way. The article says classic films are often misremembered, reduced to a few striking moments.
A motif is a recurring image, sound, or idea in a work of art. Here it means the repeated striking features people use to summarise a film instead of recalling the whole thing.
To shroud is to cover or hide, as with a cloth or mist. Here fifty years of retelling has covered the real film in myth, making it hard to see clearly.
A fable is a short story that teaches a lesson, often with invented events. Here it means the legend of how the film was made, which has blurred together with the film's own plot.
A memoir is a book in which a person writes about their own life experiences. Stallone's new memoir, The Steps, retells how Rocky was made.
Dismal means gloomy, bleak, or very poor in quality. Here it describes Stallone's unhappy childhood, before he found success.
A flophouse is a very cheap, run-down place to sleep, usually a shared room for people with little money. It shows how poor Stallone was while he studied dialogue.
Astronomical literally means about astronomy, but it is also used for amounts so huge they seem as big as the distances in space. Here it means enormous offers of money for the screenplay.
To poleax is to hit or knock down with a heavy blow, like a butcher's axe, and in everyday speech it means stunned or astonished. Here it describes Stallone, shocked as he collects the Oscar.
Lavish means rich, generous, and extravagant. Here it describes the big lapels on Stallone's jacket when he collected the Oscar.
An underdog is the person or team expected to lose in a contest. The article calls the Stallone legend one of a dauntless underdog who fights and triumphs, though the film is more nuanced.
Dauntless means fearless and determined, not discouraged by difficulty. It is used here for Stallone in the legend of how Rocky was made.
Nuanced means having subtle shades of meaning rather than being simple or black and white. The film is more nuanced than its legend suggests.
Pretentious describes someone who tries to seem more important, clever, or cultured than they really are. Here a character insists in a showy way that Rocky is not really a boxing movie.

t: happens to have boxing in it
forms: happens to have boxing in it
text: To say a film merely happens to have something in it means that thing is incidental and not the main point. The character claims Rocky is about more than boxing, and the article agrees.
Immortal means living forever. For a work of art it means so famous and loved that it will never be forgotten, like the film's horn music.
A sequel is a film or book that continues the story of an earlier one. The Rocky sequels grew sillier, with fights against Mr T and the Soviets.
Febrile literally means feverish. It also describes nervous, overexcited energy. Here it means schoolboys wound up with excitement over cartoonish fights.
To pummel is to hit again and again with fists. In the sequels Rocky pummels his opponents, which made the franchise seem much more violent than the first film.
Wallopy is an informal made-up adjective based on wallop, a hard hit. It means full of heavy punching, which is how memory paints the whole Rocky series.
To skew something is to twist it so it is no longer accurate. Stallone's later action-hero career skewed how people remembered the first film.

t: just another bum from the neighbourhood
forms: just another bum from the neighbourhood
text: A bum is an American slang word for a lazy or worthless person. Rocky's dream is only to prove to himself that he is not one, not to be world champion.
To preen is to groom yourself proudly, like a bird smoothing its feathers, and it describes someone showing off their appearance. The champion Apollo Creed is preening: vain and proud of himself.
To subsist is to stay alive with very little. Stallone once subsisted on raw eggs, a sign of how little money he had.
An enforcer is someone hired to make people obey, often by threats or violence. Rocky works as a loan shark's enforcer, collecting from people who owe money.
A loan shark lends money at extremely high interest and often uses threats to collect it. Rocky works for one.
To berate is to scold someone angrily and at length. Feeling disrespected, Rocky berates his trainer before they team up.
Wily means clever in a sly, cunning way. It describes Rocky's old trainer, who knows the tricks of the trade.
To insulate is to protect from cold or from outside effects. Paulie insulates himself with liquor, using drink as a shield against his hard life.
In music, a minor key sounds sadder than a major one. Calling a story one in a minor key means it is quieter and sadder in mood.
Looking for an angle means looking for a clever way to gain an advantage or make money. Paulie is always hunting for a scheme.
Deus ex machina is Latin for god from the machine. It is a surprise event, often lucky, that solves a problem in a story. Here the champion Creed unexpectedly offers Rocky a fight.
A fairy tale is a story with a magical, hopeful ending. The article calls Rocky a fairy tale that knows it is one.
A bigshot is an important or powerful person, often one who likes to show it. Here it is the promoter who asks Rocky about the land of opportunity.
